note: Edges from the owner's sequences catalogue that the sequence record cannot hold, because one end is a position, a movement or a grip rather than a technique. Kept here so the gap is a decision somebody wrote down. A position node on the sequence schema would let most of them in; the turnover and escape skills already cover the standard cases of 6.1 and 6.7.

sections.section: 5.2 Uke capitalises on a failed attack
edges: failed drop seoi-nage or seoi-otoshi -> uke takes the back -> sankaku-jime, koshi-jime, okuri-eri-jime, rolling juji-gatame, kuzure-kesa-gatame from the side
failed tomoe-nage or sumi-gaeshi -> uke stays on top -> pass -> yoko-shiho-gatame, tate-shiho-gatame, kami-shiho-gatame
failed kata-guruma or any low entry -> uke sprawls -> turtle attacks
failed uchi-mata or harai-goshi with tori on one leg -> uke rides down -> ushiro-kesa-gatame, kuzure-kesa-gatame
failed o-uchi-gari or ko-uchi-gari with tori on the floor -> uke on top -> tate-shiho-gatame, mune-gatame
tori pulled down from the grip -> uke passes -> osaekomi
waki-gatame from standing: recorded on the technique's contest field
standing shime-waza (okuri-eri-jime, hadaka-jime): permitted only when continued to the ground without delay

sections.shape: position (turtle) -> technique; the turnover skills cover the hold-down cases
edges: turtle -> turnover -> kesa-gatame (arm hook and roll)
turtle -> turnover -> kuzure-kami-shiho-gatame (belt or leg pull)
turtle -> turnover -> yoko-shiho-gatame
turtle -> turnover -> tate-shiho-gatame (after taking the back)
turtle -> rolling juji-gatame
turtle -> sankaku-jime (side entry), sankaku-gatame
turtle -> okuri-eri-jime, kata-ha-jime, hadaka-jime, koshi-jime, sode-guruma-jime (from behind)
turtle -> ude-garami (from the side)
turtle -> juji-gatame (from the front, arm pulled through)
turtle -> tawara-gaeshi (uke rises from the turtle)

sections.section: 6.2 From the bottom (guard, do-osae, half guard)
edges: guard -> juji-gatame
guard -> sankaku-jime -> juji-gatame -> sankaku-gatame
guard -> ude-garami
guard -> ashi-sankaku-garami (no technique record; the omoplata)
guard -> tsukkomi-jime, kata-te-jime, gyaku-juji-jime, nami-juji-jime
guard -> sweep -> tate-shiho-gatame
guard -> sweep -> kesa-gatame
guard -> hikikomi-gaeshi from ne-waza
do-jime: banned, recorded on the technique
in guard -> pass -> yoko-shiho-gatame, kata-gatame, tate-shiho-gatame, kami-shiho-gatame
in guard -> stack -> osaekomi (against juji-gatame or sankaku attempts)
ashi-garami and leg locks: banned, recorded on the technique

sections.shape: escape (a skill) -> technique; the escape skills exist and could carry a follow-up field
edges: kesa-gatame escape (bridge and roll) -> kesa-gatame reversal
kesa-gatame escape (leg trap) -> top position or ashi-gatame threat
yoko-shiho-gatame escape (bridge) -> mune-gatame or kesa-gatame reversal
yoko-shiho-gatame escape (turn to turtle) -> stand, or sumi-gaeshi from the turtle
kami-shiho-gatame escape (sit up and turn) -> juji-gatame
tate-shiho-gatame escape (bridge and roll) -> top position -> pass
juji-gatame escape (stack) -> tate-shiho-gatame or yoko-shiho-gatame
sankaku-jime escape (stack, posture) -> pass -> yoko-shiho-gatame
okuri-eri-jime escape (turn in) -> kesa-gatame
turtle escape (sit through) -> guard

sections.shape: grip-set -> technique; belongs to the kumi-kata model, not to sequences
edges: sleeve and lapel -> most forward throws
high collar or cross grip -> ippon-seoi-nage, koshi-guruma, o-soto-gari
double sleeve -> sode-tsurikomi-goshi, sode yoko-tomoe-nage
belt grip -> tsuri-goshi, ura-nage, uki-waza
back or over-the-shoulder grip -> tsuri-goshi, o-soto-gari, harai-goshi
two-on-one sleeve -> ippon-seoi-nage, sumi-gaeshi
pistol grip -> ippon-seoi-nage, sode-tsurikomi-goshi

sections.shape: variant names the catalogue uses that resolve to nothing yet
edges: ken-ken uchi-mata (the hopping continuation of uchi-mata)
sode yoko-tomoe (yoko-tomoe-nage from a double-sleeve grip)
yoko-kata-guruma and drop kata-guruma
kata-gatame-jime (the shoulder hold applied as a strangle)
ashi-sankaku-garami (the omoplata)
ouchi-gake and kouchi-gake driven through to osaekomi: the hooks exist; the drive-through is a transition already recorded
